svg.title: Italy wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: Read the peninsula from the Alps to the Mediterranean islands, keeping administrative regions distinct from individual wine denominations. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Piedmont. Northwest Italy; the Langhe/Monferrato locator is south of Turin. 2: Lombardy. Northern Italy, east of Piedmont; shown near Franciacorta, one of several distinct wine areas. 3: Veneto. Northeastern Italy, west of Friuli; several wine districts span the region. 4: Friuli. Far northeastern Italy near Slovenia; the regional heading abbreviates Friuli Venezia Giulia. 5: Trentino-Alto Adige. The Adige corridor north of Veneto; two locators distinguish Trentino and Alto Adige. 6: Tuscany. West-central Italy, south of the northern regions and west of Umbria. 7: Umbria. Landlocked central Italy, east of Tuscany. 8: Abruzzo. Central-eastern Italy, facing the Adriatic. 9: Campania. Southwestern Italy around Naples and inland Irpinia; Vulture lies in neighboring Basilicata. 10: Puglia. Southeastern Italy, including the heel of the peninsula. 11: Sicily. The large Mediterranean island southwest of Calabria. 12: Sardinia. The island west of mainland Italy and south of Corsica.

g.text: Dots: representative places · outlines: geography, not appellation boundaries

text.tspan: Explore from the Adige corridor to island shores,
one regional table at a time.
